external_theorems.citation: Z. Galil, On the complexity of regular resolution and the Davis-Putnam procedure, Theoretical Computer Science 4(1), 1977, 23-46
external_theorems.claim_used: There are infinite CNF families for which the Davis-Putnam procedure generates exponentially many distinct clauses for every variable-elimination order.

external_theorems.citation: E. Ben-Sasson and A. Wigderson, Short Proofs Are Narrow—Resolution Made Simple, JACM 48(2), 2001, 149-169
external_theorems.claim_used: For 3-regular connected expander graphs with odd charge, Tseitin contradictions are 3-CNF and require exponential-size resolution refutations.

external_theorems.citation: A. de Colnet and S. Mengel, Characterizing Tseitin-formulas with short regular resolution refutations, 2021
external_theorems.claim_used: For bounded-degree unsatisfiable Tseitin formulas, regular-resolution length is exponential in treewidth up to polynomial factors; bounded-degree expander families therefore give exponential regular-resolution hardness.

route_barrier_derivation: Each R42 Davis-Putnam elimination step materializes resolution consequences and removes one variable.

If an UNSAT trajectory reaches 2CNF, Horn, dual-Horn, or renamable-Horn with only polynomially many generated clauses and polynomial intermediate size, that terminal has a polynomial-size resolution refutation (2CNF by implication-chain resolution; Horn by unit-resolution completeness; dual/renamable Horn by the corresponding polarity transformation).
Concatenating the polynomial Davis-Putnam derivation with the polynomial terminal refutation would yield a polynomial-size resolution refutation of the original formula.
But there are 3-CNF Tseitin expander families requiring exponential resolution refutations.
Therefore no controller whose universal engine is only polynomially bounded Davis-Putnam resolution followed by these resolution-tractable terminals can be a polynomial total resolver for all 3-CNF.
